newsitem.title: USA: Kellogg opens functional foods division.
newsitem.headline: Kellogg opens functional foods division.

text.p: Kellogg Co said Monday it established a new functional foods division to focus on research, development, and marketing of foods that help consumers in the prevention and treatment of disease.

"Increasingly, medical research shows that consumption of certain nutrients can provide protection against conditions such as heart disease, high cholesterol, high blood pressure, and osteoporosis," Dr. William Mayer, president and general manager of this new business unit. "With the aging of consumers around the world, there will be an increasing demand for foods that can help prevent and manage disease."

To further research and development of innovative grain-based food products and to provide internal support for its new Functional Foods Division, the company said its $65 million W. K. Kellogg Institute for Food and Nutrition Research is scheduled to open in 1997.
Mayer joined Kellogg in 1992 and served most recently as vice president of medical affairs.
